FOR TCGPLAYER SELLERS

What TCGplayer really takes from an order.

10.75% commission on cards and the shipping the buyer pays (capped at $75 a product), plus 2.5% of the whole order — tax included — and a flat $0.30 per order. The $0.30 is per order, not per card, so the same $1 card costs 43.3% alone and 14.8% in a 20-card cart. Enter an order to see what you keep and the price that hits a profit target.

How much does TCGplayer take?

This calculator vs. tracking TCGplayer sales in a spreadsheet

Why a $1 card loses 43.3% to fees: the per-order $0.30, worked through

The order

Card price is per card; quantity is how many of that card are on the order. Shipping is what the buyer pays you on the order. Sales tax is the buyer's rate: you never receive it, but TCGplayer charges its 2.5% on it.

      Common questions

      How much does TCGplayer take per sale?

      Two fees. A marketplace commission of 10.75% of the order subtotal (cards plus the shipping the buyer pays), capped at $75 per product, and a transaction fee of 2.5% of the order total plus $0.30 per order. On a single $50 card that is $5.38 + $1.55, so you keep about $43.08 before postage and supplies, an effective 13.8%. There is no listing fee.

      Why does a $1 card lose so much to fees?

      Because the $0.30 transaction fee is charged once per order, not per card. A one-card $1.00 order pays $0.43 in fees, 43.3% of the sale. The same $1 card inside a 20-card $20 order pays $2.95 in total, 14.8%, so the order size matters more than the card price.

      Does TCGplayer charge commission on shipping?

      Yes. The commission is taken on the order subtotal, which includes the shipping the buyer pays, and the 2.5% transaction fee is charged on the whole order total including shipping and sales tax. A $20 card with $1.31 of buyer-paid shipping pays commission on $21.31, not $20.00.

      What is the TCGplayer commission cap?

      The 10.75% commission stops at $75 per product sold, which it reaches at a subtotal of about $697.67. On a single $1,000 card the commission is $75.00 instead of $107.50, so total fees are $100.30 (10.0%). Below roughly $700 the cap changes nothing.

      Did TCGplayer raise its fees in 2026?

      Yes. According to TCGplayer's fee table, the Marketplace Level 1-4 commission rose from 10.25% to 10.75% on 10 February 2026 and the per-product cap rose from $50 to $75. On a $100 card that is $0.50 more commission than the old rate. Many older calculators still show 10.25%.

      Is my data uploaded anywhere?

      No. Arithmetic happens entirely in your browser. Card prices, costs, and payouts are never uploaded. If you use the save button, your numbers are written to this browser’s own local storage on this device only, and the forget button deletes them. The optional usage counter records only which features were used and the day, never any of your numbers.

The TCGplayer $0.30 fee, and why order size decides your margin

TCGplayer's marketplace takes a 10.75% commission on the order subtotal (cards plus shipping the buyer pays) and a transaction fee of 2.5% of the order total plus a flat $0.30. The $0.30 is charged once per order, which makes the effective rate depend heavily on how many cards the buyer puts in the cart. The figures below are the same arithmetic the TCGplayer fee calculator runs; the rates are those on TCGplayer's published fee table as of its 10 February 2026 change.

Same fee schedule, different order sizes

OrderSubtotalCommissionTransaction feeYou keepEffective rate
1 card at $1.00$1.00$0.11$0.33$0.5743.3%
1 card at $2.00$2.00$0.22$0.35$1.4428.2%
1 card at $5.00$5.00$0.54$0.43$4.0419.2%
1 card at $10.00$10.00$1.08$0.55$8.3816.3%
1 card at $25.00$25.00$2.69$0.93$21.3914.4%
20 cards at $1.00 each$20.00$2.15$0.80$17.0514.8%
50 cards at $1.00 each$50.00$5.38$1.55$43.0813.8%

No buyer-paid shipping and no sales tax in these rows; postage and supplies are not deducted. Adding shipping raises the base, and tax raises the 2.5% charge, by a little.

What to do with it

If you sell many cheap singles, the price of any one card barely moves your margin; getting buyers to fill the cart does. Bulk and playset listings, a minimum-order note, and pricing the $1 cards so a typical cart clears a few dollars all work on the $0.30. At the other end, the $75 per-product cap makes expensive cards cheaper to sell as a percentage: a $1,000 card pays 10.0% all in.

The TCGplayer fee calculator runs this on your own card price, quantity, buyer shipping, tax, postage and supplies, and solves for the card price that hits a profit target. Nothing you type leaves your browser. Ranking channels for the same card? Open the where-to-sell calculator.

Common questions

What is the TCGplayer $0.30 fee?

The flat part of TCGplayer's transaction fee: 2.5% of the order total plus $0.30, charged once per order. A one-card $5.00 order pays $0.43 in transaction fees, but a five-card $25.00 order pays $0.93, only $0.50 more.

What is the cheapest card worth selling on TCGplayer?

It depends on the order, not the card. A single $1.00 card with no buyer-paid shipping keeps $0.57; if your postage is higher than that, it loses money on its own. The same card in a 20-card cart keeps $0.85 each. Selling low-value singles only pays when buyers combine them into bigger orders.

Should I charge for shipping on TCGplayer?

Shipping the buyer pays is inside the commission base, so TCGplayer takes 10.75% of it plus 2.5%. On $1.31 of shipping that is about $0.17. Charging it is almost always better than absorbing postage, but it is not free money: only about 86.8 cents of each dollar of shipping reaches you.

TCGplayer fee calculator vs. tracking your sales in a spreadsheet

This page compares two methods and names no specific product. A spreadsheet records what happened; the TCGplayer fee calculator answers what to charge before you list. Comparing channels for a card? See the where-to-sell calculator.

Where each one fits

SpreadsheetThis calculator
Best atHistory, monthly totals, tax recordsPricing one order, minimum order size, target profit
Models the $75 cap and $0.30 per orderOnly if you build itYes
Pro and pre-2026 rates side by sideOnly if you build itYes
Keeps your dataYesOnly on your device if you save

Common questions

Can I track TCGplayer fees in a spreadsheet?

Yes, and many sellers do. The catch is that the fee is not one percentage: it is a commission with a per-product cap on cards plus shipping, a second percentage on the order total including tax, and a flat charge per order, so a single "fee %" column is wrong for cheap and expensive orders alike.

When is a spreadsheet better than this calculator?

When you need history: every sale in a row, totals by month, and tax records. This calculator prices one order at a time and keeps nothing unless you save it on your own device; it is for deciding a price or a minimum order, not for bookkeeping.

What should a spreadsheet formula include?

Commission as the lesser of 10.75% of the subtotal and $75 per product, plus 2.5% of the order total (subtotal and tax) plus $0.30 once per order. Check it against one real payout before trusting it.
